name: Restaurant — full service
summary: Freestanding casual-dining / family restaurant (≈3,400–7,500 SF, 115–250 seats) with full commercial kitchen and bar. Costs are driven by kitchen MEP (hood exhaust, make-up air, grease, gas), finishes and bar build-out; site work is a smaller share than for QSR because the building is larger. Data quality is good: five 2025–2026 franchise disclosure documents (Applebee's — actual franchisee costs 2022–2024 — Chili's, Denny's, IHOP, Hooters) publish building and site ranges, plus a dated RSMeans model.

typicalSize.method: Applebee's 4,500–5,410 SF (r1); Chili's Prototype 18 4,800–5,200 SF (r2); Denny's Diner 2.0 3,400–5,200 SF, typical 4,200 (r3); IHOP 2,700–4,600 SF freestanding (r4); Hooters 5,000–7,500 SF (r5). Mid 5,000 SF.

primaryUnitsPerAcre.method: Building SF per site acre: Applebee's 4,961 SF on ~55,000 SF land (3,930 SF/ac) and 5,410 SF on ~60,000 SF (3,930 SF/ac) (r1); Denny's 4,200 SF on ~1 acre (r3, 4,200 SF/ac). Range widened ±15%.

parkingPerPrimaryUnit.method: Spaces per building SF: Applebee's ~85 spaces minimum for 4,961 SF (0.017) and ~110 for 5,410 SF (0.020) (r1). Low allows shared-parking pad sites.

perPrimaryUnit.method: Building + site work ÷ building SF. Applebee's Tower II actual franchisee costs: building $1.72–2.36M + site $168–230k on ~4,500–5,410 SF ≈ $380–520/SF (r1, 2022–2024 $); Chili's: construction $2.0–2.5M + site $0.3–1.0M on 4,800–5,200 SF ≈ $460–700/SF (r2); Denny's: building $0.95–1.5M + site $50–500k on ~4,200 SF ≈ $240–475/SF (r3); IHOP large format (3,500/4,600 SF) $1.87–3.07M incl. A&E/legal ≈ $410–880/SF, less ~6% professional services (r4); Hooters new construction $1.84–3.23M incl. architect & site on 5,000–7,500 SF ≈ $245–645/SF (r5); RSMeans 2019 restaurant model $205/SF building-only ex-architect (r6; ≈$265 in 2025 + site ≈ $310). Mid $475 ≈ median of brand midpoints (Applebee's ~$450, Chili's ~$580, Denny's ~$360, IHOP ~$600, Hooters ~$420). Low $325 ≈ RSMeans+site / Denny's low; high $700 ≈ Chili's/IHOP highs.

scope.notes: Contractor price for building (incl. kitchen hoods/exhaust, bar millwork, restrooms) and on-site work (paving/parking, utilities to building, lighting, landscaping). Excludes kitchen & bar equipment, furniture, sound/TV, signage, POS (ffe), land, soft costs, liquor license, impact/tap fees.

qualityTiers.method: economy ≈ low/mid (Denny's-type family dining, 325/475 ≈ 0.68–0.72); premium ≈ high/mid (Chili's/IHOP upper ranges, 700/475 ≈ 1.47 → 1.3 for standard-high casual dining); luxury 1.8 = polished casual / fine dining with custom interiors (not sourced; verify).

systemSplit.method: Site (31–33) = 0.18 from franchisor splits: Applebee's site 168–230k of 1.89–2.59M (9%, r1), Chili's 0.3–1.0M of 2.3–3.5M (13–29%, r2), Denny's 50–500k of 1.0–2.0M (5–25%, r3) → mid ~17–18%. Building 0.82 allocated with a restaurant elemental pattern (MEP 22+23+26 ≈ 28% for kitchen loads; finishes 10%; GCs 9%). No published elemental estimate found.

lineItems.name: On-site work (utilities to building, parking paving, curbs, lighting, landscaping)

cost.method: Applebee's Tower II $168,274–$230,269 (r1); Chili's pad site $100–150k + landscaping $20–60k, 'up to $1,000,000 for a full site' (r2); Denny's $50,000–$500,000 (r3). Mid ≈ $350k for a raw-but-flat outparcel.

lineItems.name: Outdoor dining patio (slab, rail/fence, shade, heaters, lighting)

cost.method: Derived: patio slab/pavers + fencing + shade/heaters priced as a fraction (~20–40%) of the interior dining-room $/SF mid ($475). Verify with a local quote.

lineItems.notes: Many prototypes include a patio; add when the program calls for one.

perPrimaryUnit.method: Kitchen/bar equipment + furniture + signage + POS per SF: Applebee's FF&E & signage $1,220,400–$1,348,864 / ~5,000 SF = $244–270 (r1); Chili's kitchen/bar equip $400–600k + furniture/sound/TV $140–175k + signage $50–160k + accessories $50–60k = $640–995k / 5,000 SF = $128–199 (r2); Denny's EF&F $350–450k + signs $80–120k + tech $25–40k = $455–610k / 4,200 SF = $108–145 (r3); Hooters new $630–865k / 6,250 SF = $100–138 (r5). Mid = median ≈ $165.

pctOfHard.method: Applebee's professional services $123,725–$143,261 + permits/fees $26,000–$28,900 on $1.89–2.59M (≈6–8%, r1); Chili's pre-construction $75,000–$350,000 on $2.3–3.5M (3–10%, r2); Denny's A&E $30–60k on $1.0–2.0M (3%, r3). Add legal, insurance during construction, testing, PM, utility deposits → mid 12%.

softCosts.notes: Type-specific soft items: liquor license (Hooters lists $300–$10,000 in non-quota states; quota-license states can run six figures — verify locally), initial franchise fee $30,000–$60,000 (Denny's $30k; Chili's $40–60k; IHOP/Hooters $50k) for franchised builds.

design.method: Prototype-based restaurants carry modest design contingency; custom independents toward the high end. Judgment.

hard.method: Restaurant industry guidance of 10–15% total project contingency (retail-pad-qsr.json#e10) split into design + hard.

perPrimaryUnit.method: Hard $325–700/SF × (1.08–1.18) ≈ $350–830/SF; widened to $950 for small-footprint high-cost (IHOP 2,700 SF prototype implies $667–947/SF incl. professional services, r4). Excludes land and FF&E.

evidence.quote: Total Building Cost $219.52/SF (union) incl. Contractor Fees (25%) $41.03/SF and Architectural Fees (7%) $14.36/SF; 'uses 2019 RSMeans data'.
evidence.scopeNotes: Value = $219.52 − $14.36 = $205.16/SF; 5,000 SF single-story model, building only, no sitework or kitchen equipment. Open shop total $199.37.

openQuestions: Independent (non-franchise) full-service restaurant costs in urban markets likely exceed franchise prototypes; a public city-owned restaurant lease/build budget would help.
No sourced elemental (CSI) breakdown — systemSplit is derived.
Liquor license cost varies by state quota system; not modeled numerically.
